stories.title: JLL Secures $40M Refinancing for Multifamily in Portland’s Lloyd District
stories.excerpt: JLL has secured a $40.5 million refinancing for The Payton, a 162-unit multifamily property in Portland, Oregon. JLL represented the borrower, ColRich, in arranging the five-year, floating-rate loan through Prime Finance. The Payton, located at 2020 NE Multnomah St., is a seven-story mid-rise community built in 2019. JLL Capital Market’s Debt Advisory team was led by Senior Managing Director Aldon Cole, Managing Director Jimmy Conley, Directors Brock Knapp and Sean O’Brien, and Analysts Ben Choromanski and Matthew Payamps. The property sits at the confluence of Portland’s Central Eastside and Lloyd District, two of the metro area’s most centralized urban submarkets, with over five million square feet of retail within one mile. The property maintains 98% occupancy as of August 2026. “The successful refinancing of The Payton demonstrates the positive momentum in Portland’s multifamily market and the quality of ColRich’s long-term ownership strategy,” said Cole. The post JLL Secures $40M Refinancing for Multifamily in Portland’s Lloyd District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL refinanced The Payton, 162-unit Portland property, $40.5M floating-rate loan.
Lloyd District/Central Eastside submarket asset maintains 98% occupancy as of Aug 2026.
Prime Finance provided five-year term; mid-rise built 2019 in dense urban node.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged a $40.5 million five-year floating-rate refinancing for The Payton, a 162-unit mid-rise apartment community in Portland's Lloyd District delivered in 2019. The property maintains 98% occupancy and sits at the confluence of two central urban submarkets with over 5 million square feet of retail within one mile. The transaction was placed through Prime Finance and signals lender confidence in Portland's multifamily fundamentals.
stories.impact: Refinancing activity at near-full occupancy and strong debt execution in Portland's urban core suggests stabilized fundamentals and lender appetite for quality mid-rise assets in that submarket. Lloyd District's density and retail proximity position new development favorably for Class A rents and value-add plays, particularly for mixed-use projects that can capture synergies with surrounding retail and office.

stories.title: Cushman & Wakefield Arranges $37M Financing for MD Mixed-Used Development
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has arranged $37.37 million in floating-rate construction financing for Derby Place, a 94,587-square-foot retail development anchored by Whole Foods Market in Bel Air, Maryland. The property is already 92% committed with retailers and service providers. Located at 610 Baltimore Pike, Derby Place will feature 60,000 square feet of luxury boutiques, restaurants, shops and amenities. The development will offer 512 parking spaces on a 10.45-acre site. Derby Place will replace a vacant Macy’s location at the former Harford Mall. Cushman & Wakefield’s Equity, Debt & Structured Finance team of John Alascio, Mark Gilbert, Alex Hernandez, and Mitch Rothstein represented the borrower, SJC Ventures, in securing the financing. SJC Ventures recently began the demolition process of the former Macy’s. Bank of America provided the loan. “This transaction exemplifies the continued demand for institutional-quality, grocery-anchored retail in high-barrier markets,” said Gilbert. The post Cushman & Wakefield Arranges $37M Financing for MD Mixed-Used Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: C&W arranged $37.37M construction financing for Derby Place retail in Bel Air, Maryland.
Project 92% pre-committed; Whole Foods-anchored, replaces vacant Macy's at former Harford Mall.

stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield secured $37.37 million in floating-rate construction financing for Derby Place, a grocery-anchored retail development in Bel Air, Maryland anchored by Whole Foods with 92% tenant commitments. The project replaces a vacant Macy's location and will feature 60,000 square feet of luxury retail, restaurants, and shops on a 10.45-acre parcel. Bank of America provided the loan as SJC Ventures began demolition.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; however, grocery-anchored mixed-use redevelopment of regional mall sites signals real estate's shift toward neighborhood convenience and experiential retail, which can create foot traffic and amenity pull for nearby residential development. The strong pre-leasing (92% committed) in a repurposing scenario demonstrates demand for curated retail experiences in suburban nodes, validating co-located residential strategies in secondary markets.

stories.title: Fortress Refinances Dania Design Center With $45M After Foreclosure Fight
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Fla., following a nasty foreclosure fight with its previous owner, New York-based billionaire Charles Cohen. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $45 million loan backing the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex at 1855 Griffin Road, facing the I-95. In the past two years, Fortress has invested about $3 million updating the campus, which dates back to 1988. Another $3 million to $5 million of renovations are planned over the coming year. In June, it tapped Jamestown to oversee management and leasing of the mixed-use property. The move comes about five years after the Design Center lost one of its main tenants, online pet retailer Chewy, which occupied about 100,000 square feet, when it relocated to Plantation Pointe. Fortress won control of Design Center and the neighboring Le Méridien Dania Beach hotel in 2024, through a $76 million credit bid. The proceeding was part of a broader foreclosure suit with Cohen Realty Enterprises, which Charles Cohen’s father Sherman Cohen had founded in the 1950s. In 2022, the New York-based lender provided a $535 million debt package, covering several commercial properties, including Cohens’s Dania Beach assets. The billionaire also personally guaranteed a $187 million portion of the loan. A year later, Cohen defaulted, prompting Fortress to take control of the commercial real estate. The lender also went after the borrower’s personal assets, believing the commercial properties were worth less than what Cohen owed, the Wall Street Journal reported. These include a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferraris. In response, Cohen sold off several properties in New York. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgement. But the legal battle remains, with Cohen filing to recoup $204 million in alleged damages. The 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex has received $3 million in updates since acquisition, with another $3–5 million planned. Jamestown was tapped in June to oversee management and leasing.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development; however, the Fortress-led repositioning of distressed office-showroom assets in South Florida's industrial corridor (near I-95, Dania Beach) signals broader capital availability for mixed-use and office-to-alternative-use conversions in the region. If Design Center moves toward hospitality, flex, or creative office as leasing stabilizes, it could influence competing capital deployment and land values in adjacent submarkets where multifamily developers operate.

stories.title: MDH Partners Acquires 1M-SF Industrial Building in Indiana
stories.excerpt: MDH Partners (MDH) has acquired 70 Connect III, a 1,005,776-square-foot industrial building in Greenfield, Indiana, part of the Indianapolis metropolitan area. The building, developed by Lauth, was delivered on a speculative basis and sits along West 350 North in the East industrial submarket. JLL represented the seller in the transaction. MDH’s Director of Acquisitions Houston Hawley led the acquisition for the firm. JLL’s Brian Buschuk and Brian Seitz will handle leasing for MDH. “We’re ultimately believers in quality assets at a good basis, and that’s exactly what we’re getting with 70 Connect III,” Hawley said. The cross-docked building offers 40-foot clear heights, 108 dock doors expandable to 216, four drive-in doors, an ESFR sprinkler system and eight-inch slabs. The site has two points of entry along West 350 North and is less than three miles from Interstate 70 and about ten miles from Interstate 465, Indianapolis’ primary loop. The Indianapolis International Airport and its FedEx hub are within a 30-mile drive. stories.title: Keystone Equities Provides $61M Acquisition Debt for IOS Repositioning Site in Newark
stories.excerpt: KS Group has secured $60.5 million in acquisition debt to buy a 51-acre industrial site in Newark, N.J., that will be repositioned as an industrial outdoor storage property, Commercial Observer can first report. Keystone Equities provided the debt, structured as a senior bridge loan, marking $660 million in capital the firm has deployed since August 2023, the firm noted in a release. KS Group is buying the site from an ownership group led by Daryl Hagler. CBRE’s Shlomo Weissberg and Eli Klapper arranged the transaction. Jonathan Zamir, founder and CEO of Keystone Equities, noted in a statement that the site is currently under active environmental remediation and still hadn’t secured a certificate of occupancy before closing, which led to several “traditional lenders” to decline to underwrite the risk associated with the deal. “This was a deal that required real diligence. We dug in, structured around the risks, and found a solution that works for both us and the borrower,” he said. “That’s where Keystone adds value.” Located at 151 Raymond Boulevard in Newark, the industrial site is a former PSEG property that holds proximity to Port Newark-Elizabeth and New York City. The new IOS site will include parking for both trucks and trailers, a container garage for shipping, and electric vehicle and solar charging stations. CBRE noted in recent reports that IOS vacancy in Northern New Jersey stands at 2.5 percent, while rents have grown 123 percent since 2020. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Keystone Equities provided $60.5M senior bridge for KS Group's 51-acre Newark industrial-storage repositioning.

stories.summary: Keystone Equities provided a $60.5 million senior bridge loan for KS Group to acquire a 51-acre industrial site in Newark, New Jersey that will be repositioned as an industrial outdoor storage property. The site is currently under environmental remediation and lacked a certificate of occupancy at close—conditions that disqualified traditional lenders. The transaction marks $660 million deployed by Keystone since August 2023.
stories.impact: Keystone's willingness to deploy bridge capital into remediation-stage Newark industrial land signals recovery and development activity in distressed North Jersey corridors. For multifamily developers, this underscores available specialty debt capital for complex risk structures and suggests increasing investment velocity in Newark's industrial and mixed-use zones, which could drive land values and labor availability for residential projects in nearby submarkets (Jersey City, Newark core, Ironbound).

stories.title: CMBS Special Servicing Rate Dips in July as Office, Lodging Improve
stories.excerpt: The Trepp CMBS special servicing overall rate declined 11 basis points in July to 11.09%, partially reversing the increases of recent months. However, decreases in special servicing rates were not seen across the board in all property types. The improvement was led by office, the largest special servicing category, along with lodging, whose rates fell 53 and 26 bps to 16.58% and 8.63%, respectively. Industrial edged down three bps to 1.34%. That progress outweighed a sharp increase in retail, where a heavy wave of regional-mall loans transferred into special servicing for maturity default, lifting the retail rate 33 bps to 13.28%, Trepp reported Multifamily rose 16 bps to 8.39%, and mixed-use edged up two bps to 11.93%. New transfers to special servicing totaled roughly $1.69 billion across 41 loans and were unusually concentrated in retail, which accounted for about $903.6 million. The flow was dominated by regional malls reaching their balloon maturities. The post CMBS Special Servicing Rate Dips in July as Office, Lodging Improve appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trepp CMBS special servicing rate fell 11 bps in July to 11.09%; office down 53 bps to 16.58%.
Multifamily special servicing rose 16 bps to 8.39%; mixed-use edged up 2 bps to 11.93%.
Retail spiked 33 bps to 13.28% as regional malls hit balloon maturities; $1.69B new transfers overall.
stories.summary: The Trepp CMBS special servicing overall rate declined 11 basis points in July to 11.09%, driven by marked improvements in office (down 53 bps to 16.58%) and lodging (down 26 bps to 8.63%). However, multifamily special servicing rates rose 16 basis points to 8.39%, while mixed-use ticked up 2 basis points to 11.93%. Retail saw the sharpest increase—up 33 basis points to 13.28%—as regional mall loans transferred into special servicing for maturity defaults.
stories.impact: Rising multifamily special servicing rates (up 16 bps to 8.39%) signal emerging credit stress in certain multifamily CMBS pools, likely concentrated in markets with softening fundamentals or aggressive leverage. This suggests tightening CMBS availability for multifamily transitional deals and cap-rate compression opportunities in secondary markets; well-capitalized developers should monitor distressed CMBS pools and maturing debt in supply-constrained metro markets (Sunbelt growth cities, tight suburban rings) for acquisition targets.

stories.title: Return to Lender: Week of August 13, 2026
stories.excerpt: An out-of-state hedge fund has won an auction to acquire the entirety of Spirit Airlines’ former headquarters in South Florida with a $93.25-million cash bid. The South Florida Business Journal reported that the now-defunct carrier named DPC HoldCo LLC, an affiliate of Boston-based Hill City Capital, as the successful bidder in a notice of auction results. Hill City was also the stalking horse bidder in the auction, which was brokered by Savills Eastdil Secured. A downtown San Antonio office building, anchored by La Panaderia Bakery & Café on the ground floor, has sold in a distressed sale. The Vogue Building at 600 Navarro St. traded in an Aug. 5 foreclosure auction for about $5.2 million, the San Antonio Business Journal reported. Ownership entity Vogue SATX LLC, connected to local investor Dr. Sanjay Misra, defaulted on a $6 million loan drawn up by Blue Sky Bank. The bank took control of the property, which was last appraised at $6 million, per the Bexar Central Appraisal District. U.S. National Bank Association, the lender for Denver’s tallest tower, has requested a receiver for the property after ownership defaulted on an approximately $130-million loan, reported the Denver Business Journal. Republic Plaza, at 370 17th St., is owned by Brookfield Properties and insurer MetLife. The retail space at Brightline MiamiCentral Station could be seized in a $65-million foreclosure lawsuit, according to the Orlando Business Journal. U.S. Bank, acting as administrative agent for two groups of lenders, filed a foreclosure complaint July 30 against Brightline Investment Holdings and DTS DT Retail LLC, along with property manager FECI Realty. The roughly 124,000 square feet of retail at 600 N.W. 1st Ave. is owned by DTS DT Retail, which is a subsidiary of Brightline Investment Holdings. stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Relocates to 5K SF at GFP’s 515 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Zimmet Law Group is relocating its practice inside Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet signed a 5,476-square-foot lease for a newly completed space inside GFP Real Estate’s 515 Madison Avenue, also known as the DuMont Building. Located at the corner of East 53rd Street, the 42-story office tower is just one block south of Zimmet’s current abode in RFR Holding’s 477 Madison Avenue. Zimmet’s practice areas range widely, from matrimonial and family law to real estate matters. The law firm was represented by Savitt Partners’ Elliot Zelinger, while GFP’s Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone negotiated in-house for the landlord. Zelinger did not respond to a request for comment. Asking rent for the nearly 10-year lease term was not disclosed, but office asking rents in Midtown averaged $88.50 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Cushman & Wakefield data. Zimmet is expected to take occupancy at 515 Madison later this year, according to GFP, following the completion of its new space. Zimmet’s office did not respond to a request for comment on the relocation. Earlier this year, GFP took full ownership of the 350,000-square-foot Class A tower after securing an $86.5 million refinancing deal with Apple Bank, which enabled the buyout of ATCO Properties & Management’s remaining 40 percent stake in the property. By late February, the landlord had secured 12,000 square feet of new leasing activity, Commercial Observer reported. GFP announced another 9,000 square feet of deals in late July, including leases for investment firm T7 Capital, aesthetic training provider Innovation Training Specialist and Widowski Law Group. Other tenants at 515 Madison include alternative asset manager Whitebox and therapy provider Manhattan Psychiatry Group. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group leased 5,476 SF at GFP's 515 Madison Avenue (Midtown Manhattan).

stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group signed a 5,476-square-foot lease for a newly completed space at GFP Real Estate's 515 Madison Avenue (the DuMont Building) in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from a nearby address. The nearly 10-year lease is priced at market Midtown asking rates averaging $88.50 per square foot as of Q2 2026. The firm is expected to take occupancy later in 2026.
stories.impact: Not relevant to multifamily development; office leasing activity in Plaza District does not directly signal residential demand or supply dynamics. However, ongoing office tenant stability and new lease activity in Midtown East suggest selective office market recovery in prime Manhattan addresses, which could support mixed-use and residential development in transit-adjacent Midtown submarkets if office demand stabilizes further.

stories.title: Sixth Street Acquires Iconic Pier House Hotel in Key West for $190M
stories.excerpt: An iconic luxury hotel in Key West, Fla., is changing hands. Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital have acquired Pier House, a longstanding 142-room oceanfront resort in downtown Key West, from Braemar Hotels & Resorts in a $190 million deal, according to a release from Sixth Street. Starwood Property Trust provided the debt financing, the amount of which has not been disclosed, while the Plasencia Group advised Braemar Hotels & Resorts on the sale. Aman Gupta, principal at Sixth Street, noted in a statement that Pier House has access to a private beach and includes unobstructed sunset views for its guests while also being in the heart of Downtown Key West. “This investment reflects Sixth Street’s commitment to identifying high-quality hospitality assets where we can drive long-term value,” said Gupta. Located at 1 Duval Street, Pier Street sits on five acres of beachfront land along the famous Duval Street, a top tourist destination and walkable retail and entertainment thoroughfare. The resort first opened in 1967 and had been owned by Braemar Hotels & Resorts since 2014. On-site amenities include two oceanfront restaurants, a spa, a fitness center, an oceanfront pool and 3,000 square feet of event space. “We believe Pier House represents an opportunity to acquire a historic luxury resort in one of the country’s most supply-constrained and sought-after tropical leisure markets,” said Gupta. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital acquired Pier House Resort (Key West) for $190M.

stories.summary: Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital acquired Pier House, a 142-room luxury oceanfront resort in Key West, Florida from Braemar Hotels & Resorts for $190 million. The property sits on five acres of beachfront at 1 Duval Street, a prime tourist and retail destination with private beach access and unobstructed sunset views. Starwood Property Trust provided debt financing.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; however, strong institutional capital (Sixth Street) acquiring iconic hospitality assets at premium valuations in Key West signals confidence in Florida's experiential tourism and short-term rental dynamics. For multifamily developers, this underscores potential for adaptive-reuse and conversion opportunities in similar high-amenity coastal markets, and validates mixed-use strategies that blend residential, hospitality, and retail in destination submarkets with limited supply.

stories.title: Heights Advisors Files Plans to Build 606 Affordable Units in the Bronx
stories.excerpt: Heights Advisors, a Brooklyn-based development and investment firm led by founder and president Rachel Foster, is planning to bring 606 affordable housing units to the Bronx’s Soundview neighborhood. The firm filed a land use application Wednesday with the New York City Department of City Planning requesting a zoning amendment and a special permit to build a 21-story mixed-use building with 606 units at 945 White Plains Road. The filing initiates a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), which typically takes about seven months of public review of the proposed zoning changes, and includes formal hearings before a final vote by the City Council and City Planning Commission. If approved, Heights Advisors’ proposed project would span 515,063 square feet and include 503,095 square feet of residential space and 11,968 square feet of commercial space, the application notes. The Brooklyn developer is seeking construction financing under the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development’s New Construction Finance Program, which provides funding for the construction of 100 percent affordable multifamily rental projects, according to the filing. Of Heights Advisors’ 606 planned units, approximately 152 are set to be affordable. It’s unclear whether Heights Advisors, which is the ground lessee of 945 White Plains Road on a 99-year ground lease, plans to demolish the current retail property on the site, which is home to a Modell’s Sporting Goods and GameStop. Heights Advisors did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. Other residential developments planned for the Bronx include a 228-unit affordable senior housing development at 3728 Park Avenue, as well as a pair of 99-unit residential buildings at 761-769 East Tremont Avenue. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Heights Advisors, a Brooklyn-based developer, filed a land-use application with NYC Department of City Planning for a 21-story mixed-use building with 606 affordable units at 945 White Plains Road in the Bronx's Soundview neighborhood. The 515,063-square-foot project includes 503,095 square feet of residential and 11,968 square feet of commercial space. Heights Advisors is seeking construction financing through HPD's New Construction Finance Program, with the ULURP process expected to take approximately seven months.
stories.impact: New York City's aggressive affordable housing pipeline in Bronx growth corridors (Soundview) signals sustained demand for workforce multifamily and HPD-financed development in outer boroughs. This validates development strategies targeting mixed-income and naturally-occurring affordable housing in Bronx neighborhoods with transit access and infrastructure investment. For developers, HPD's financing availability for large-scale projects and Soundview's emerging status as a growth node make the submarket relevant for community-based partnerships and affordable-focused acquisition strategies in the coming 12–24 months.
